field.label: Enabled
field.help: Switched off, the rule does nothing, and keeps its place.

field.label: Action
field.help: Block: a block rule of this plugin's on the application's table, from the source alone and ahead of the rules of Firewall: Rules, so a new connection from there to a server in the table is dropped; the connections nDPI names as the application from there cut, some 10 to 70 seconds after they began - in hardware too, where os-xgs-npu is installed with Cut in hardware on; and a Suricata rule that drops them in the Intrusion Detection's IPS mode and alerts in its IDS mode. Alert: a Suricata rule that alerts on them, nothing blocked.

field.label: Source
field.help: The devices the rule is for: any, an interface's network - the guest network, say - an alias, or an address or a network. Not the firewall itself nor one of its addresses: no device connects through it from there.

field.label: Invert source
field.help: Every device but those of the source: a block for every device except one, say. One item only.

field.label: Application
field.help: As the installed nDPI names it. A protocol that carries others - TLS, QUIC, HTTP - takes every application it carries. Suricata matches the names nDPI knows the application by, and its protocol when Suricata reads that protocol itself; one it can tell by neither gets no Suricata rule, and the rest still acts.

field.label: Description
field.help: For your reference; Suricata's alerts carry it too.
